name: Tessera Corponation Cenotaph Burst Transmitter — 'The Epitaph'
product_name: Tessera Corponation Cenotaph Burst Transmitter — 'The Epitaph'
description:
The Cenotaph Burst Transmitter is a single-use emergency communications device — a hardened cylinder approximately the size of a flare, designed to transmit one compressed message packet across a maximum possible range before destroying itself. Tessera Corponation developed it for deep-cover operatives and isolated field agents who needed a last-resort option when all other communication had failed. The device charges over a period of 60–90 seconds from activation, during which it compresses, encrypts, and fractures the stored message into a multi-frequency burst transmission that fires simultaneously across forty-three frequency bands in a single 0.008-second pulse.

The burst is, by design, impossible to miss and impossible to trace. The transmission is so brief that direction-finding equipment cannot lock a bearing before it ends; the multi-frequency fracturing means no single monitoring system captures the complete message; and the device physically incinerates its own internals after firing, leaving a slag of ceramic and fused circuitry that yields nothing recoverable. Recipients must have a Tessera Cenotaph receiver unit — a small passive module that captures and reconstructs burst fragments across all forty-three bands simultaneously — to decode the message. Without a paired receiver, the burst is unintelligible noise across dozens of bands.

The Epitaph's cultural weight comes from its irreversibility. A device that destroys itself after a single transmission, designed for use when everything else has failed, carries an unmistakable implication. Tessera markets it to corporations for deniable deep-cover operations; the black market sells it to anyone who thinks they might someday need to scream once, very loudly, and then disappear. In GLMZ intelligence circles, receiving an Epitaph burst from a contact is understood to mean one of two things: either they've gone dark permanently, or whatever they've just told you is the most important thing they'll ever say.
legality: Prohibited (civilian); Licensed (corporate and government intelligence operations)

specifications.message_capacity: Up to 4 minutes compressed audio or equivalent data
specifications.encryption: Paired asymmetric key, hardware-bound to receiver unit
specifications.self-destruction: Complete internal thermal incineration within 2 seconds of transmission
specifications.detection_resistance: Very high — burst duration prevents direction-finding; multi-band fracturing defeats single-system capture

tactical_use: The Epitaph is a last-resort or planned-exfiltration tool. Operatives carry it when entering situations where all other communication might be compromised or where a single guaranteed transmission is worth more than ongoing contact. Common uses include: transmitting final intelligence from a compromised position, sending an exfiltration call that cannot be jammed or intercepted, or delivering a pre-composed message on a timer if the operative fails to abort the sequence. The 60-90 second charge window is the critical vulnerability — the device must be activated in advance of the moment transmission is needed. Skilled operators pre-charge the Epitaph before entering a potential compromise situation.
cultural_context: In GLMZ, the Epitaph has become something of a dark legend — less a piece of equipment than a ritual object. Finding one on a dead operative tells you they died before they could use it; finding the slag of a fired one tells you they did. Intelligence professionals discuss them in hushed, almost superstitious terms. There is a known practice among some deep-cover operatives of recording a personal message on their Epitaph at the start of an assignment — not operational intelligence, but something personal — to be transmitted if they trigger it under duress. Whether this message reaches anyone depends entirely on whether their handler is still monitoring the receiver frequency. Some are not.
known_users: Corporate intelligence assets in hostile territory
Handlers and cutouts managing isolated assets
GLMZ resistance cells as exfiltration triggers
story_hooks: A Cenotaph burst is received by a dormant receiver unit in the players' possession — from a contact they believed dead for over a year. The message is fragmented, partially corrupted, and ends mid-sentence.

Someone in the city is firing Epitaphs on a schedule — one every seventy-two hours for the past three weeks. The transmissions are addressed to a receiver that no longer exists. Someone needs to find out who is sending them and why before Tessera Corponation's signals division does.

The players are given an Epitaph pre-loaded with a message they are not permitted to read. Their job is to get it to a specific location and fire it. Whether they follow those instructions is another matter.

A slag-form Epitaph is recovered from a crime scene. Tessera Corponation wants it back — not because of what it was, but because the self-destruction mechanism on this batch was defective, and the internal records may be partially recoverable.

physical_description.visual_profile: A hardened cylindrical emergency transmitter resembling a high-grade flare or signal cartridge. The form factor is deliberately military-industrial: compact, purposeful, built for grip. The casing tapers slightly at both ends, with a recessed activation cap at the top. Visually austere — no unnecessary ornamentation. It reads as a device designed to be deployed, not displayed.
physical_description.dimensions: 18cm length × 3.5cm diameter — handheld, pocket-sized with effort, easily carried in a tactical vest pouch or field pack
physical_description.weight_description: 300 grams — light enough to pocket, substantial enough to feel engineered. Pocketable but not weightless; the heft conveys precision manufacturing
physical_description.primary_material: Aerospace-grade composite ceramic-reinforced titanium alloy casing with internal ablative shielding
physical_description.finish: Matte, non-reflective industrial gray with subtle heat-treatment discoloration along the mid-barrel. Texture is slightly rough, tactile, purposefully un-polished. Designed to resist fingerprinting and thermal imaging
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal gray primary with black anodized aluminum activation collar. Accent: a single narrow band of deep indigo near the top, marking the Tessera Corponation proprietary encryption standard (visible only at certain angles)
physical_description.interface_elements: Recessed twist-lock activation cap (requires two-handed engagement to prevent accidental trigger). No visible screen or display—the device is entirely passive until armed. A small pressure-release valve near the base (barely visible). No indicator LEDs. When armed, a faint amber glow emanates from a thin line around the activation collar during the 60–90 second charge cycle—the only feedback mechanism
distinctive_features: Thermally-etched serial number on the barrel (unique to each unit, laser-burned deep into the metal)
A hairline fracture pattern etched into the lower third of the casing—decorative but functional, marking stress-relief points that guide thermal destruction
Subtle Tessera Corponation logo (three interlocking squares forming a tessellated pattern) embossed on the collar, filled with metallic ink that catches light at specific angles
Slight bulge at the mid-point where the capacitor banks sit—creates an almost organic, stressed curve to the cylinder
The top cap bears a tiny recessed groove for a fingernail or tool—no button, deliberately tactile and deliberate
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: TESSERA CORPONATION — etched in small sans-serif caps below the logo. A regulatory stamp (GLMZ-certified, non-recoverable ordnance classification). Batch code and manufacturing date laser-printed on the base in near-invisible gray-on-gray
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine, handled sparingly. Field units show slight surface oxidation or scratches from gear contact. Units in actual use are rare; most observers never see a fired Epitaph (only the residue—fused slag). A pristine unit suggests someone who hasn't needed to scream yet

Overhead key light emphasizes the matte gray finish and thermally-etched details. A second rim light from the left catches the indigo proprietary band and creates subtle highlights along the edge, revealing the faint fracture-pattern etching.
